title: Always Tired and Sluggish When Dieting: A Sign You're Eating Too Little?
intro: Usually, yes. Extreme tiredness when dieting is a sign you've cut your food too much and too fast. With a small deficit and enough protein and carbs, you can still lose weight and have energy for work.

sections.p: Dizzy in the afternoon, hard to focus in meetings and quick to get angry. You may also always feel cold and have trouble sleeping. Some people overeat when they get home at night. If these signs happen almost every day, your diet may be too strict.

To lose an estimated 0.5-1 kg a week, cut an estimated 300-500 kcal from your daily needs. Don't cut drastically to below 1,200 kcal without professional guidance. Cutting a little but consistently works better than cutting a lot but not being able to keep it up.
Carbs are the main energy source for your brain and muscles. Take half to one scoop of rice at lunch at the nasi campur, and add dishes and vegetables. You can still lose weight while eating rice.
Protein helps you stay full longer and protects your muscles. Choose eggs, chicken, fish, tempeh, tofu or dhal. A breakfast of two eggs, or bread with egg, keeps you full much longer than kuih alone.

sections.h: Not all tiredness is from dieting
sections.p: Lack of sleep, work stress, low iron and thyroid problems can also make you sluggish. If the tiredness continues even though you're eating enough, or your period suddenly becomes irregular, see a doctor for a check-up.

action: Write down everything you eat for 3 days to see whether you're eating too little.
Add one protein source to every meal this week.
Bring back half a scoop of rice at lunch if you've dropped rice for a long time.
Prepare a small snack for 3-4 pm, for example a banana and a handful of nuts.
Go to bed 30 minutes earlier on at least 3 nights this week.
myth: Many people believe the hungrier you are, the more fat you burn. In reality, extreme hunger makes you sluggish, move less and overeat easily at night. A moderate deficit is easier to maintain.

faq.q: Can I eat very little on workdays, then eat more on weekends?
faq.a: Possibly, but many people end up overeating on weekends until the weekday deficit disappears. It's more comfortable and stable to eat moderately every day.

faq.q: If I'm tired, should I stop exercising completely?
faq.a: No need. Lower the intensity for a week or two, for example walking or light exercise. At the same time, fix your eating and sleep first. If you feel like fainting or have chest pain, stop and get a doctor's advice.

faq.q: I often feel dizzy during my period. Is that because of my diet?
faq.a: Many factors can be involved, including loss of blood and iron. Make sure you eat enough, and talk to a doctor if you get dizzy often or your period is very heavy.
